title: Choose a research method
summary: Match the decision and question to the evidence a method can produce.
steps: Name the decision, its owner, the population and the uncertainty that matters.
Use prototype usability or implementation A/B testing for observed task behavior; use a preference test for preference. Preference does not establish task performance.
Use card sorting to explore grouping and labels; use tree testing to assess findability. Grouping alone does not establish findability.
Use surveys or interviews for reported experience and explanations. Reported intention is not observed completion.
Record alternatives and limits. Moderated sessions, interviews, field work and some accessibility studies need methods outside the unmoderated Studio runner.
questions: Which outcome answers the question, and what can this method not establish?
example: To learn whether people interpret a waiting status correctly, score their interpretation. A click event alone does not answer that question.

sources.title: Team research handbook; adapted from the HF795 study-design and survey materials
